question: Will the Bank of Canada decrease the target for the overnight rate by 25 bps at the October interest rate announcement?
scope: Factual inputs only; no forecast or outcome assessment. Frozen rule asks for a rounded 25-bp decrease bucket, not any-size cut; upper bound applies if rate is a range; sub-25-bp movements round to 25; emergency changes outside the announcement are excluded. Postponement/cancellation terms remain as frozen.
facts: Latest official BoC decision before the scheduled October announcement: on 2026-09-02, target held at 2.25% (Bank Rate 2.50%; deposit rate 2.20%). BoC named 2026-10-28 as next decision.

BoC calendar lists 2026-10-28 and 2026-12-09 as remaining 2026 decisions; announcement time is 09:45 ET. October decision coincides with Monetary Policy Report. The Sep2 record and calendar are the available official target/calendar facts as of capture; no October outcome is implied.

BoC Governing Council summary for Sep2 decision was published Sep16. It describes Q2 growth 3.3%, excess supply, unemployment around 6.5%, subdued wage growth, CPI near 3% with gasoline/energy pressure, and competing inflation-upside versus weak-growth/trade-uncertainty risks. This is a retrospective account of Sep deliberations, not an October forecast.

Statistics Canada Sep2026 CPI release (published Oct19): all-items CPI +3.1% y/y versus +3.0% in Aug; CPI excluding gasoline +2.2% versus +2.4%; all-items +0.1% m/m (seasonally adjusted +0.4%). The release states the next CPI release, for Oct, is Nov16. Thus an ‘Oct20 CPI’ was not upcoming as of Oct20; latest CPI release then was Sep reference month. No consensus-surprise claim: no original forecast survey sourced.

Statistics Canada Sep2026 Labour Force Survey released Oct9; reference week Sep13–19. Employment fell 68,000 (−0.3%); employment rate −0.2 pp to 60.6%; unemployment +0.1 pp to 6.5%. No original forecast-survey surprise sourced.

Latest formal monthly GDP-by-industry release captured: July2026, published Sep29; real GDP was essentially unchanged in July. The same release's advance estimate for Aug was +0.2%, provisional and scheduled for update Oct30; distinguish it from the formal July result. No survey surprise sourced.
